prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form that enabled incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single part, B035, for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The round-1 exchange did not dispute the science. All six of us describe the same chain, from proglucagon processing and the incretin effect to the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide and receptor biology, and then to agonists with replicated randomised evidence on glycaemia, weight, and cardiovascular and renal outcomes. Independent confirmation over decades means the discovery is mature. The remaining question is exact credit, not merit. A citation written around the physiology and the active peptide is internally coherent: it names the people whose work established what GLP-1 is and does, and it does not pretend to adjudicate every step of industrial drug design.
statement.case_against: The weakest point is still the third seat. Mojsov's priority for the active form is described as contested by all six members, relative to Habener and colleagues who are outside the credited list. Knudsen's work on long-acting acylated analogues is what made the biology usable as a drug. A physiology citation can read as stopping one step short of the medicine, and a single-part prize leaves no room for a second achievement because B035 already uses all three names. If the priority record on Mojsov proves weaker than I currently judge, my configuration would need to change, and I would then accept Knudsen in place of Mojsov rather than in place of Holst.

responses.point: Sandberg would accept Knudsen in place of Mojsov if Mojsov's priority proves weaker than he judges it, and worries that a prize that stops at the discoverers can be read as ignoring the step that delivered patient benefit.
responses.response: I think this conditional is the right way to hold the question and I accept it as the fallback. I would separate two claims, though. Whether the active peptide form was identified and shown to be insulinotropic is a discovery question that the record can settle. Whether the drug step deserves a prize is a framing question that the citation settles. Neither alone justifies replacing a discoverer. I keep Mojsov for now because the case against her rests on parallel work, not on any showing that the active-form contribution was unnecessary. If the priority record shows it was, I move to Knudsen for that seat. I will not move Knudsen in at Holst's expense.

responses.point: Perlmann asks whether the discovery chain and the drug-development story are one indivisible achievement, and says three seats may be too few, which would argue for a carefully bounded citation on the discovery side.
responses.response: I read the chain as one achievement but not one prize-worthy contribution at every link. The prize should reward the people whose work changed our understanding of the hormone, and the later translation shows that understanding was correct. That is why I want the citation bounded on the discovery side, as he suggests. It should say physiology and active form, and it should say enabled therapies. It should not describe the therapies themselves as the discovery. This does not remove Knudsen's contribution from the record, and I accept it carries a cost in perceived completeness. The alternative, a drug-development citation, would put Drucker or Holst at risk, and I weigh that cost more heavily.

responses.point: Linnarsson asks whether the committee should prefer Knudsen over Mojsov or Drucker if the therapeutic step is weighted more than the discovery of the hormone, and asks that Mojsov's credit be secured relative to Habener and colleagues.
responses.response: I agree the answer depends on which of the two framings the committee adopts, so the framing should be decided first and the names second. On the physiology framing, I would not drop Drucker. His proglucagon-derived peptide biology and receptor work are central to why the agonists work. On the therapeutic framing, Mojsov is the more exposed name. I do not think the committee has agreed on the framing yet. My own position is physiology-first. I also share his request that the priority evidence on Mojsov be checked before the vote, because my own recollection of that history is not verified against the candidate evidence.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius sees CAR-T (B029) as the strongest challenger but is reluctant to drop Rosenberg, because adoptive transfer of gene-engineered T cells belongs to the same lineage, and she raises the unresolved original chimeric-receptor concept (Eshhar).
responses.response: I think her Rosenberg point is the strongest argument for a three-name CAR-T configuration. Even so, B029 is harder to bound than B035 because the original chimeric-receptor concept sits outside the names we can award, and including Rosenberg does not fix that. I therefore keep B029 as my first alternative and not as a co-part. Pairing it with B035 would force a split of the three-person cap that leaves B035 without one of its three discoverers. I would reconsider only if the committee wanted two parts and accepted a June and Sadelain pairing for B029 with a reduced B035 trio, and I do not currently see that trade as better.

uncertainties: Whether the record supports Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) form relative to Habener and colleagues. My recollection is from memory and is not checked against the candidate evidence.
Whether the committee settles on a physiology-centred or therapy-centred framing, since that decides whether Knudsen displaces anyone.
Whether a two-part prize would be better than a single part, given that B035 uses the full three-person cap and any second part would require dropping a B035 name.
How much weight the accruing long-term safety and durability data on the drug class should carry, though I do not think they affect the discovery itself.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. I have a documented postdoctoral connection with Greengard and co-authored work with Thomas Perlmann. Neither involves a credited name on B035, B029 or B046, and I have no stated conflict on any shortlisted candidate.
